messages:
Nina: Heads-up: we need final customer comms for the network-degradation incident. Ops says we have a confirmed timeline but legal wants clarity on RCA access.
Carlos: I can put together a short status update for the public page and a slightly longer customer email. Prefer to avoid technical jargon.
Priya: Legal: for customers with contract clauses wecan share the detailed RCA. For public channels we should use a redacted summary that covers impact, root cause summary, mitigations, and next steps.
Ben: Ops: confirm whether any requests returned errors vs retries. That changes the suggested wording about "possible duplicate responses."
ops-bot: Metric check complete: total 502 errors peaked at 03:14 UTC, ~37k requests retried. No auth failures observed.
Nina: Good. Public-friendly line: "brief service disruption in us-west resulting in elevated latency and some failed requests between 03:10	6:00 UTC. We resolved the issue by rolling back a config change and rewarming caches." Keep it short.
Priya: Add explicit line: "No customer data was exposed." Legal insists.
Carlos: Draft status page snippet: "Resolved: elevated latency and intermittent request failures in us-west (03:10	6:00 UTC). Cause: transient network instability affecting cache priming. Impact: some requests failed or were retried; no data exposure. Action: config rollback and cache persistence; full follow-up planned." Thoughts?
Ben: Sounds fine. Suggest adding: "We're scheduling a targeted reliability review to address recurring network flaps" to show were taking systemic action.
Nina: Agree. Also need clear who sends detailed RCAs to customers on contracts. Support should own distribution, engineering owns the content, legal signs off.
Carlos: I'll mark engineering as content owner. Priya, can legal sign off by EOD tomorrow if we send a draft?
Priya: Yes, if the draft is provided by EOD today. For high-touch customers we'll attach the full timeline, mitigations, and technical appendix.
Nina: Action items: 
- Ben (Ops): paste final timeline + retries/error counts into the postmortem (by 13:00 PT).
- Carlos (Product): publish status page copy and customer email template (by 18:00 PT).
- Support: prepare affected-customer list and distribution plan (by COB).
- Priya/Legal: review detailed RCA and approve distribution list (by next business day).
- Nina: open infra follow-up ticket for reliability review (owner: Nina, due in 7 days).
ops-bot: Note: this is the 3rd network-related incident in the past 10 weeks in us-west. Recommend an aggregated incident review.
Ben: I'll add a monitoring alert that increments a rolling counter for network flaps over 14 days. If it exceeds 2 we trigger an on-call review.
Carlos: For public readability: avoid blaming vendors. Keep phrasing neutral: "transient external network instability" -> maybe "intermittent upstream network instability"? Priya: we prefer "upstream network instability" is OK.
Nina: Make sure the status page links to the support article on safe retry patterns. Also include a contact route for customers who report duplicates.
Carlos: Will include link + support email.
Priya: One more policy item: let's document in the postmortem which customers received the full RCA and the approval chain. That helps audits.
Nina: Agreed. Add that to the incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4210/actions
Carlos: Posting draft to #incidents-drafts for quick review. Please add inline comments.
Ben: Once timeline is in, I'll verify the mitigation language matches the steps we took (rollback, cache persist, alert tuning).
Nina: Thanks everyone. Plan: public status page tonight, targeted full RCAs to affected contract customers after legal approval tomorrow. We'll follow up with the aggregated reliability review next week. :thumbsup:
